newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums ease in absence of buyers.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums ease in absence of buyers.

text.p: Thai raw sugar FOB premiums eased further in the absence of buyers, trade sources said.
Thai raw sugar premiums for January-March 1997 delivery are being quoted at around 1.0-1.05 cents over New York March futures contracts, they said on Thursday.
Ample stocks in China, one of Asia's major buyers, and better crop prospects in leading exporting countries such as Australia, Brazil, South Africa and Thailand pressured premiums.
"China overbought last year. And another bad news is its sugar output this year could be one of the highest on record," said a trader from one London-based trading house here.
China's state-run Xinhua news agency said output could soar to as much as 2 million tonnes.
At Thai ports, sugar vessel movements remained slow without any new declarations. As of Thursday, about 42,000 tonnes of white and raw sugar were shipped or scheduled to be shipped.

The vessel Panoramos Bay left Thailand on September 19 for Kuwait with 5,000 tonnes of bagged white sugar. E.D & F Man was the buyer. The Pipob Samut left on September 20 with 16,600 tonnes of bulk raws for Japan, while Tate & Lyle and Kerry were also said to have bought 17,650 tonnes of bulk raws for Japan. The Vala Navee was slated to leave Thailand September 25.
